title_primary: Local demographic reorganization does not imply a transferable island-resilience rule in Antarctic penguins
title_alternative: Local island reorganization does not yield a transferable demographic rule across Antarctic penguin populations
fit_rationale: The manuscript explicitly links biology to geography at nested local-to-continental scales.
It tests a clearly framed island-ecology hypothesis rather than documenting a taxon-specific pattern.
The conceptual contribution is a boundary on transferability: ecological information can be real within islands without transferring through static island descriptors across populations.
The Antarctic-wide component is comparative across three Pygoscelis species, while the Palmer component provides a local discovery system rather than the sole evidentiary basis.
Title wording uses 'does not imply' rather than an absence claim because the MDE analysis leaves moderate cross-species effects unresolved.
editorial_risk: Editors may view the Antarctic-wide primary result as non-confirmatory and ask whether the paper is sufficiently biogeographical rather than demographic.
The manuscript must therefore foreground the cross-scale information-transfer question, not penguin natural history.
Do not oversell radius variation as scale dependence; the frozen joint null p=0.0810 specifically prevents that framing.
Do not imply absence of moderate effects; MDE80/MDE90 show limited sensitivity near the observed effect size.
cover_letter_angle: The paper uses an unusually stringent nested design to ask when island-level ecological information transfers across scales. A strong local within-island phenomenon survives fixed-composition/count-error nulls, whereas the corresponding Antarctic-wide static-island rule does not survive preregistered cross-species inference. The contribution is the demonstrated boundary between local explanatory structure and transferable biogeographical structure.

prohibited_pitch: A positive option-fragmentation crossover was discovered.
The study proves island architecture does not matter.
